overall_summary: Deduplicated analysis reveals a clear performance divergence: visceral first-person hypothetical survival scenarios ('What If You Fell Into...') and extreme planetary hazards dominate viewership (800–1,050+ views, 3.5%+ like ratios), whereas abstract cognitive psychology and repetitive trivia topics severely underperform (<100 views, 0–1% engagement). Videos optimized between 19–21 seconds significantly outperform 12–16 second uploads in algorithmic pickup.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) deliver 5x–10x higher traction than third-person descriptive titles.
winning_patterns.action: Frame extreme cosmic or environmental phenomena through second-person immersive survival scenarios ('What happens to your body if...').

winning_patterns.pattern: 20–21 Second Pacing Window with Visceral Science
winning_patterns.evidence: Top 5 non-outlier performers average 20.4 seconds with dense cause-and-effect pacing, while sub-16s shorts stall below 150 views.
winning_patterns.action: Script precisely for a 20–21 second runtime, pacing 3 escalating physical consequences before a final mind-bending revelation.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5–53 views), 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' (38 views), and song-loop videos failed repeatedly.
weak_patterns.action: Retire isolated neuro-trivia shorts unless anchored to high-stakes survival or visceral biological horror.

weak_patterns.evidence: Repeated uploads of 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' and 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' flatlined with diminishing returns.
weak_patterns.action: Enforce strict uniqueness rules; expand into unvisited cosmic entities and extreme geological phenomena rather than recycling past scripts.
